content.value_statement: Async Python code can leak sessions, block responses, and deadlock under load. This skill gives FastAPI and SQLAlchemy patterns for safer async database work.
actual_capabilities: Shows when to use concurrent or sequential database queries.
Describes transaction commit, rollback, and refresh patterns.
Covers connection pool and session closure pitfalls.
Provides background task and deadlock avoidance guidance.
Lists local checks for session leaks and missing awaits.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a runnable library.
Examples must be adapted to each project schema and session factory.
Detection commands are heuristic and may miss project-specific issues.
It focuses on FastAPI and SQLAlchemy, not every async framework.

use_cases.title: Improve FastAPI Database Endpoints
use_cases.description: Use request-scoped sessions, safe commits, and refresh patterns while building async API handlers.

use_cases.title: Review Async Query Performance
use_cases.description: Decide which queries can run concurrently and which queries must stay sequential because of data dependencies.

use_cases.title: Investigate Async Production Issues
use_cases.description: Trace session leaks, connection timeouts, stale data, deadlocks, and slow endpoints with focused async patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Async Session Scope
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a FastAPI endpoint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use py-async-patterns to explain how this FastAPI endpoint should scope AsyncSession usage. Identify any session leak risks.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Transaction Boundaries
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate refactor for writes that must succeed together.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use py-async-patterns to review this async database write flow. Recommend commit, rollback, refresh, and transaction boundary changes.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Query Concurrency
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced performance review for read-heavy endpoints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use py-async-patterns to classify these async queries as independent or dependent. Suggest where gather is safe and where await order matters.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Async Failure Modes
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced reliability review before production release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use py-async-patterns to audit this service for session leaks, pool exhaustion, stale data, deadlocks, and missing post-condition validation.

output_examples.input: Review an async FastAPI handler that creates a record and returns it immediately.
output_examples.output: The review explains where the session should be scoped, where commit belongs, and why refresh is needed before returning generated fields.

output_examples.input: Assess a dashboard endpoint with several database reads.
output_examples.output: The answer separates independent reads from dependent reads, then recommends safe concurrency only for queries that do not share results.

output_examples.input: Investigate a timeout in an async API under load.
output_examples.output: The response lists likely session leaks, connection pool pressure, and missing closure points to inspect first.

best_practices: Scope each AsyncSession to one request or unit of work.
Use explicit transactions when several writes must succeed together.
Validate async post-conditions before returning user-facing results.
anti_patterns: Using a global shared AsyncSession across requests.
Running dependent database queries concurrently before required data exists.
Starting fire-and-forget tasks without considering error handling.

faq.question: Does this skill run code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation patterns and optional local diagnostic commands for users to review.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on FastAPI, SQLAlchemy AsyncSession, asyncio, and common async database workflows.

faq.question: Can it replace project-specific database tests?
faq.answer: No. Use it to guide implementation and review, then verify behavior with your own tests.

faq.question: Does it cover connection pooling?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains session closure, pool exhaustion symptoms, and NullPool tradeoffs for async usage.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it during reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Is it useful for production incidents?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps triage common async failures such as stale data, deadlocks, and slow endpoints.
